record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Counting periodic bands in irrational polygons
record.original_question: For an irrational polygon P, let f_P(ℓ) denote the number of periodic bands of billiard orbits of length at most ℓ. Find nontrivial upper and lower bounds for f_P(ℓ).

evidence.quote: Denote by fP (￿) the number of periodic bands of length at most ￿. This is a counting function of periodic orbits in polygons.
Problem 11. Find nontrivial (upper and lower) bounds on fP for irrational polygons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a polygon P in the Euclidean plane and the billiard dynamics inside P (a point particle moving in straight lines and reflecting elastically off the sides, with behavior at vertices left undefined). Call P irrational if at least one of its interior angles is not a rational multiple of π. A periodic billiard orbit comes in a maximal parallel family ("periodic band") consisting of all parallel periodic orbits of the same combinatorial type and length. For ℓ > 0, let f_P(ℓ) denote the number of periodic bands of billiard orbits in P of length at most ℓ.

Establish nontrivial upper and lower bounds, as functions of ℓ, for f_P(ℓ) valid for every irrational polygon P (or for natural classes of irrational polygons).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding sharp upper and lower bounds for the counting function of periodic bands in irrational polygons remains open. Partial results exist: there are irrational polygons whose counting function grows superlinearly (faster than n log^k n for any k on an open set of polygons), and examples with upper bounds of the form R log^k R. No general nontrivial bounds applicable to all irrational polygons are known.

status_evidence.title: Lower bounds on growth rates of periodic billiard trajectories in some irrational polygons
status_evidence.snippet: There exist irrational polygons in which the number of periodic billiard paths of length less than n grows faster than n log^k n on an open set of polygons.
status_evidence.claim: Partial lower bounds known for special families of irrational polygons; no universal bounds.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (R. E. Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Very little is known about counting periodic trajectories in irrational polygonal billiards.
status_evidence.claim: General problem of bounding f_P for irrational polygons remains open.
